### nc-review: comments — 1 important, 5 nits

@pcbeingused333 — a few things worth a look, none blocking.

The PR makes the `subscribe:` parser strict: each trigger kind now has an allowed-key list, and any other key throws `SubscribeParseError` with a "Did you mean" hint, which fixes the silent widening described in #2247 for both the single-file frontmatter path (error logged, file loads without triggers) and the bundle `skill.yaml` path (surfaced as a manifest parse error). The four per-kind cases are covered by tests that would fail without the fix, and the changeset is present and correctly named. It is not ready as-is because the new key lookup crashes on kinds that collide with `Object.prototype` members instead of producing the intended validation error.

**🟠 important · `correctness` · `source/skills/parse-subscribe.ts:130`**

`KIND_KEYS` is a plain object literal, so `KIND_KEYS[kind]` walks the prototype chain. For a kind such as `toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf` or `__proto__`, `own` is a function (or `Object.prototype`), not the `undefined` the guard expects:

```ts
const own = KIND_KEYS[kind];
if (!own) return; // unsupported kind: reported by the caller
const allowed = [...COMMON_KEYS, ...own];
```

`own` is truthy, so the guard does not fire and the spread throws `TypeError: own is not iterable`. `parseSubscribeBlockOrWarn` only swallows `SubscribeParseError` and rethrows everything else, so this `TypeError` escapes `parseCommandFile` / `parseCustomToolFile` / `parseSubagentMarkdown` — the whole member fails to load with `Failed to load custom command from ...` instead of the file loading with its triggers dropped, which is the behaviour the issue asks for. The manifest path degrades less badly (`bundle-loader.ts` catches it and reports `errorMessage(err)`), but the message is still a raw `TypeError` rather than "kind is not a supported event kind".

Fix by not trusting the prototype chain, e.g. `const own = Object.hasOwn(KIND_KEYS, kind) ? KIND_KEYS[kind] : undefined;` (or use a `Map`), or by moving the `assertKnownKeys(obj, kind, index)` call to after the kind is validated against the four supported kinds.

**⚪ nit · `design` · `source/skills/parse-subscribe.ts:113`**

The allowed-key lists duplicate a shape that already exists in two other places: the `SkillTrigger` union in `source/types/skills.ts` (`paths`, `eventKinds`, `cron`, `branches`) and the per-kind parsers in this same file (`parseFileChanged`, `parseFileAiComment`, `parseScheduleCron`, `parseCiJobFailed`). Adding a new filter key now means editing three places, and missing one makes a previously valid configuration fail to load with "unknown key" — the whole `subscribe:` block is dropped, so the trigger silently stops firing. `file.ai-comment` was added recently, so this is not a hypothetical drift. Consider deriving the allowed keys from the trigger types, or at least a comment on `KIND_KEYS` pointing at `source/types/skills.ts` as the source of truth.

**⚪ nit · `design` · `source/skills/parse-subscribe.ts:151`**

This is the third hand-rolled `editDistance` in the tree — `source/cli-args.ts:35` and `source/input/unresolved-file-mentions.ts:267` already have private copies (and `source/cli-args.ts` also carries a `findSuggestion` helper with the same "did you mean" shape). A shared `source/utils/edit-distance.ts` would avoid a fourth copy drifting. Not a blocker, but `source/utils/` is the bottom layer for exactly this kind of helper.

**⚪ nit · `tests` · `source/skills/parse-subscribe.spec.ts:178`**

The new tests only exercise `parseSubscribeBlock` directly. The PR description makes two behavioural claims that no test pins: that a bundle `skill.yaml` with an unknown key reports the error as a manifest parse error (`SkillManifestParseError`, which is what `manifest-parser.ts` does with a `SubscribeParseError`), and that a single-file member with an unknown key still loads with its triggers dropped. The second path is covered incidentally by the existing `parser-subscribe-integration.spec.ts` case for a different malformed input; the manifest path is not covered at all. One case in `manifest-parser.spec.ts` (an unknown key in `skill.yaml`) would pin both the claim and the error type.

**⚪ nit · `completeness` · `source/skills/parse-subscribe.ts`**

Outside the issue's scope, but in the same symptom class: `paths: []` is still accepted and still widens to "every file". `parseFileChanged` stores the empty list, `registrar.ts` copies it into `filter.paths`, and `matchesFilter` in `source/events/event-router.ts` only applies the glob filter when `filter.paths.length > 0`, so a zero-length list means "match everything" — the same widened trigger the issue is about, reached by a different route. Worth a follow-up issue rather than a change here.

**⚪ nit · `design` · `source/skills/parse-subscribe.ts:139`**

The hint branch ends the message with `?` while the caller appends a period, so the logged line reads `Invalid subscribe block in <path>: subscribe[0] has unknown key "path" for kind "file.changed". Did you mean "paths"?. Loaded without triggers.` Dropping the trailing `?` from the template (or the `.` from the wrapper) removes the double punctuation.

---

<sub>🔴 blocking · 🟠 a reviewer would ask for a change · ⚪ optional</sub>

<sub>Automated code review — correctness, security, design, tests, plus duplicates and scope. A human still decides; this is not a substitute for review and is not exhaustive. The required status checks separately cover lint, formatting, types, unused dependencies, the test suite and the build. This bot never merges. Maintainers can rerun with `/re-review`.</sub>
Thanks @pcbeingused333, merged! Appreciate the clean fix and the per-kind allow-list with the "Did you mean" hint.
